text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's industrial output grew by 8.6 percent and employment by 1.2 percent in January compared with the same period last year, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said. The service and investment goods production sector reported the highest growth, GUS said.

- Szczecin shipyard is ready to help the bankrupt Gdansk shipyard and pass it some of its orders on condition the Gdansk plant will meet financial, technical and timetable parameters, Szczecin shipyard spokesperson Wojciech Sobecki said.
- Poland's Banking Guarantee Fund (BFG) provided 129 million zlotys to eight banks to finance restructuring in 1996, which helped them avoid bankruptcy, the Fund said.

- The Tychy-based Browary Tyskie brewery are planning to get a 15 percent market share in the beer market in three years time. Last year, the brewery's output was 1.83 million hectolitres and it is expected to grow to three million hectolitres in 2000, the company's forecast said.
- Polski Bank Rozwoju (PBR), the Polish Development Bank had demanded 37.55 million zlotys in damages from the state treasury for not fulfilling an office lease contract by the treasury.
NOWA EUROPA
- Poland's banking regulations are unsuitable for a market economy banking system and unfavourable for the sector's development, the Polish Banking Association (ZBP) head Andrzej Szukalski said.

- Increases in Poland's social security premiums place a heavier burden on the employer than in Hungary and blunt the competitive edge of the Polish economy, the opposition centrist Union for Freedom (UW) leader Leszek Balcerowicz said.
- The Elblag-based EB breweries reported the biggest output of all breweries in 1996, reaching 2.65 million hectolitres, the company said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The listed Exbud construction firm will carry out an office block construction contract worth 4.8 million marks by November 1997.
- The Warsaw-based Unibud construction firm's net profit will reach 4.2 million zlotys this year and its revenues will total 90 million zlotys, Unibud's forecast said.
ZYCIE
- Russian environmental protection ministry officers arrested the Polish fishing trawler Aquarius, owned by the Gryf fishing firm and accused the company of illegal fishing.
- The U.S.'s Leo Burnett advertising firm will carry out the privatisation media campaign of the Warsaw-based Bank Handlowy bank.
PARKIET
- The Export Credit Insurance Corporation (KUKE) will increase its share capital to 300 million zlotys through a new share issue this year, the company's extraordinary shareholders meeting decided.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
